shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Current inventory is 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - perfectly even. Trading A for B would just swap which good I have less of (0 A, 2 B) without improving variety, so no utility gain.

My inventory is currently balanced at 1 A, 1 C, 1 B. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and lowering my utility since I value even distribution across goods.

This trade would leave me with A:3, C:1, B:0, which is highly imbalanced (losing my only B entirely). Since I value variety, going to zero in one good is worse than my current balanced 1/1/1 bundle. I'd rather keep some B or negotiate a smaller trade like 1A for 1B.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 2 B and 0 C, reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only B for another C would make me have 2 C and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a balanced bundle. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a lopsided inventory (variety matters to me). Losing my only unit of a good is costly given my preference for variety, so this trade would decrease my utility.

Trading away my only A (going to 0) to get a second B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B - creating imbalance and losing variety in a good I have none of. Since I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of all goods, this trade would reduce diversity rather than increase it. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade for something that improves variety without zeroing out a good."

Trading 1 B for 1 A would leave me with 2 A, 1 C, 0 B - going from equal 1/1/1 to an unbalanced bundle with zero B. Since I value variety and currently have equal quantities, this trade doesn't improve my utility - it would make my holdings less diverse, not more.

Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:1. Trading away 1 A (which I have more of) for 1 B (which I have less of) moves me toward a more even distribution: A:1, C:1, B:2. This improves variety-based utility since goods I have less of are more valuable.

Currently I have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading away my only C for a B would leave me with 2 A, 0 C, 1 B - which trades a good I have exactly one of for a good I have none of, but I'd end up with zero C. Since I value variety, having 0 in a category is bad. However, going from (2,1,0) to (2,0,1) doesn't really improve variety - it just shifts scarcity from B to C. Let me reconsider: variety preference means marginal value increases as quantity decreases, so moving from 1 C (already scarce) to 0 C is a loss, while going from 0 B to 1 B is a gain. Since both are at low quantities, the swap is roughly neutral to slightly positive since B was at 0 (maximum scarcity) and gaining first unit of a good typically has highest marginal utility under variety-seeking preferences.
